profile.summary: ProtSSN scores the effect of amino acid substitutions on a protein without any experimental training data for that protein (zero-shot). It takes a protein sequence together with its 3D structure as a PDB file and returns a fitness score for each listed mutant. It combines a protein language model for the sequence with a graph neural network over the structure, and needs no multiple sequence alignment.

summary_quotes.text: Fusion of protein **sequence and structural** information, using **denoising** pre-training network for **protein engineering** (**zero-shot**). Please note that we do not require MSA or evolutionary information.
Because our model requires **structure (PDB)** as input
this article introduces a novel pre-training framework that integrates sequential and geometric encoders for protein primary and tertiary structures.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each protein is turned into a k-nearest-neighbour graph over its residues. A frozen ESM2-t33 language model supplies the node features, and a six-layer equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) learns from the structure. Pre-training is a denoising task: residues are randomly mutated at each epoch to imitate natural mutation, and the model learns to recover the wild type. Variant effects are then scored from the model's fitness for the mutated sequence. The authors describe the method as an adapter that strengthens a language model, and the language model can be swapped.

ProtSSN utilizes noise sampling at each epoch on the node attributes to emulate random mutations in nature.

This framework guides mutation directions toward desired traits by simulating natural selection on wild-type proteins and evaluates variant effects based on their fitness to perform specific functions.
You can view our work as an **adapter** to enhance the capabilities of language models, so you can replace any language model as a prefix.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Nine checkpoints are released, one for each combination of graph size k (10, 20 or 30 neighbours) and hidden size h (512, 768 or 1280). They are named k10_h512 to k30_h1280. They can be used alone or averaged as an ensemble; the developers recommend k20_h512 when using one model. A result should name the checkpoint, or the list of checkpoints in the ensemble. The Hugging Face repository was at revision cb2d622f when read.

sections.title: Inputs and data preparation
sections.body: Each protein needs a folder with its PDB structure and a TSV file of mutants. Multiple mutations in one variant are joined with a colon, for example M1V:A2V. The developers suggest predicting the structure with AlphaFold or ESMFold, or downloading it from the AlphaFold database. A helper script builds all single-point saturation mutants for a protein that has no experimental data.

run_guide.summary: Set up the environment, download one checkpoint, and score the example ProteinGym mutant set with a single model.
prerequisites: Anaconda3 or Miniconda3, as the README requires for the conda environment.
A GPU with at least 10GB of memory for inference, such as an RTX 3080, per the README's Hardware section.
A PDB structure and a TSV mutant file per protein; the repository ships an example set under data/mutant_example.
The code is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial use and no derivatives.

notes: Two doubts for a reviewer. First, the licence: the repository LICENSE and README say CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, while the Hugging Face card for the checkpoints says apache-2.0; both are recorded and neither is resolved. Second, the README's zero-shot command calls zeroshot_predict.py, which does not exist at commit 9da358e2, so the run guide uses compute_fitness.py from script/compute_fitness.sh at the same commit and the swap of k20_h512 for k10_h512 in the download step is disclosed. The repository is now ai4protein/ProtSSN while the Hugging Face checkpoints and the paper's citation use tyang816; the paper's Data availability section names the ai4protein repository. Parameter counts are read as millions from the paper's Table 1 header, since the README table gives no unit. The records for this model and for VenusREM or VenusFactory lines mentioned in the README News section may overlap.
